text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The chairman of the cabinet committee on the economy, Cassim Chilumpha, said the government would have to halve the 100,000-strong civil service if it were to implement recommendations of an independent commission of inquiry that it raise civil service wages by 100 percent.
- The Supreme Court of Appeal rejected an appeal by the attorney-general to throw out of court a case over the status of member of parliament Fred Nseula, who changed parties.
- Malawi was isolated from the international community when aircraft could not land nor take off from the airport following a massive strike by civil servants which has entered its second week.
